subject: GPS satellite
title: Your GPS Would Drift 10 Kilometers a Day Without Einstein

scenes.text: Your GPS would be wrong by ten kilometers a day without Einstein.
GPS satellites orbit about 20,000 kilometers up, where gravity is weaker, so their clocks tick faster than clocks on the ground.
Their speed slows them down a little, but gravity wins. The net result is about 38 microseconds faster every day.
That sounds tiny, but GPS finds you by timing radio signals that travel at the speed of light.
Left uncorrected, the error would grow by around ten kilometers every single day.
So engineers set the satellite clocks slightly slow before launch. Einstein is built into your map.

description:
Your GPS would be wrong by ten kilometers a day without Einstein.
GPS satellites orbit about 20,000 kilometers up, where weaker gravity makes their clocks run faster than clocks on the ground. Even after their speed is accounted for, the net gain is about 38 microseconds a day, and since position is found by timing light-speed signals, the error would grow by around ten kilometers daily. Engineers correct it by setting the satellite clocks slightly slow before launch.
Did you know your phone uses relativity?
